questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum of Functions With Constant Factors
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we convert the radical into a rational exponent, and we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}-5x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2/3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2/3})-5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}^{(\frac{2}{3}-1)}-5\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}^{-1/3}-5 \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{x}}-5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum of Functions With Constant Factors
questions.worked_solution:
Here, we apply the addition, constant multiple, and power rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-3{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{-2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{3/4}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2})-3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3/4}) \\  & =2\cdot (-2){x}^{(-2-1)}-3\cdot \frac{3}{4}{x}^{(3/4-1)} \\  & =-4{x}^{-3}-\frac{9}{4}{x}^{-1/4} \\  & =-\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{9}{4\sqrt[4]{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum of Functions Without Constant Factors Using the Sum Rule
questions.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is the sum of three power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =3{x}^{(3-1)}+(-2){x}^{(-2-1)}-1 \\  & =3{x}^{2}-2{x}^{-3}-1 \\  & =3{x}^{2}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Negative Power Function Using the Constant Multiple Rule
questions.worked_solution:
We first rewrite the function as

$$
y=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}=\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3/2}.
$$

Then, we apply the constant multiple and power rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-\frac{3}{2}){x}^{(-\frac{3}{2}-1)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-5/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum of Functions Without Constant Factors Using the Sum Rule
questions.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$  is the sum of two power functions. So, we apply the sum rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4/3}) \\  & =5{x}^{(5-1)}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{(4/3-1)} \\  & =5{x}^{4}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{1/3} \\  & =5{x}^{4}+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
